title: Short-Circuit Logic: Conditional Right-Operand Evaluation
description: LogicOp node type with eval_logic that evaluates left first, then conditionally evaluates right. and: if left truthy, evaluate right; else return left. or: if left truthy, return left; else evaluate right. Bomb class proves right side skipped: and False Bomb() returns False without explosion; or True Bomb() returns True. Real guard: i < len(items) and items[i] > 0 safely returns False for out-of-bounds i.
source: draft: omp free model + edit: codex + check fix: claude

steps.description: LogicOp node: stores operator ('and'/'or'), left and right child nodes.
truthy helper: converts value to bool (Python semantics).

eval_logic: evaluates left. For 'and': if truthy(left), evaluate right and return it; else return left. For 'or': if truthy(left), return left; else evaluate right and return it. This IS short-circuit: right evaluated only when needed.
and logic: left evaluated first. If falsy, return left immediately (short-circuit). If truthy, evaluate right and return its value (value-preserving).
Bomb class: any evaluation raises RuntimeError. evaluate_demo handles literals, Bomb, LogicOp. Proves short-circuit by constructing LogicOp with Bomb as right child.

steps.question: What does evaluate_demo(LogicOp('and', False, Bomb()), {}) return, and does Bomb explode?
steps.answer: Returns False. Bomb does NOT explode because left is falsy, so right is never evaluated (short-circuit).

steps.description: Test 1: and False Bomb() -> False (no explosion). Test 2: or True Bomb() -> True (no explosion). Test 3: and True Bomb() -> explodes as expected (left truthy forces right eval).
Real guard idiom: items contains the supplied values, and i=5 is out of bounds. i < len(items) and items[i] > 0 returns False safely because left is False, so items[i] never evaluated.
Output: False, True (short-circuit works, Bomb not evaluated)
Output: as expected: the right side was evaluated! (for and True Bomb()); Safe guard result: False
